title: Governor of Pennsylvania

context.text: Incumbent Democrat Josh Shapiro is seeking a second term. Shapiro and Republican state Treasurer Stacy Garrity each won their party's May 19, 2026 primary unopposed.

Lieutenant governor nominees are chosen separately in the primaries and run jointly with the governor in the general election: Austin Davis (D) with Shapiro, and Jason Richey (R), who won the Republican primary over John Ventre 65.6% to 34.4%, with Garrity. The Libertarian Party nominated Ken Krawchuk for governor and John Thomas for lieutenant governor.

Green Party candidates Tony Dastra and Craig Bolton were ruled off the general-election ballot by a Commonwealth Court judge because Dastra did not have enough valid signatures; Dastra said he plans to campaign as a write-in. Spotlight PA reports that Libertarian Ken Krawchuk is the only third-party candidate for governor on the ballot, and Adams County's official November 3 ballot lists only the Shapiro, Garrity and Krawchuk tickets for governor.

candidates.name: Josh Shapiro
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. Austin Davis. Advanced unopposed from the May 19 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Education funding, tax relief and workforce development, as described in his statement on signing the FY2025-26 budget.
priorities.quote: In a divided legislature, we proved once again that Democrats and Republicans can come together to get stuff done for the good people of Pennsylvania — cutting taxes, investing in education and workforce development, supporting law enforcement and reducing crime, and keeping our economy growing.

priorities.text: Raising Pennsylvania's minimum wage to $15 an hour, which he again urged lawmakers to pass in his February 2026 budget address.
Protecting access to abortion in Pennsylvania.
priorities.quote: as long as I'm Governor, abortion will remain safe, legal, accessible here in our Commonwealth

positions.summary: Says he will veto any effort to restrict reproductive freedoms and has directed state agencies to expand access; joined the Reproductive Freedom Alliance of governors in February 2023.
positions.quote: I've made very clear that I will veto any effort to restrict women's reproductive freedoms

positions.summary: Called on the legislature in his February 2026 budget address to raise the state minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 an hour.
positions.quote: Raising the minimum wage to $15/hour will save this commonwealth $300 million a year on entitlement programs like Medicaid

record.text: Signed the $50.1 billion FY2025-26 budget, which created the Working Pennsylvanians Tax Credit (an earned income credit equal to 10 percent of the federal credit), raised public school adequacy funding by $565 million and included cyber charter school funding reform.

Joined the Reproductive Freedom Alliance with other governors in February 2023 and maintained an executive order protecting non-residents seeking abortion care in Pennsylvania from arrest or detention at another state's request.
Proposed a $53.2 billion FY2026-27 budget that renewed his call for a $15 minimum wage.

candidates.name: Stacy Garrity
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Jason Richey, Allegheny County Republican chair. Advanced unopposed from the May 19 Republican primary.

priorities.text: Keeping taxes down while 'raising hope,' according to her campaign website.
priorities.quote: Stacy Garrity will be a Governor more interested in raising hope, than raising our taxes.

priorities.text: Expanding natural gas development to supply energy and data centers, and ending the state park and forest drilling-lease moratorium.
priorities.quote: We will utilize the God-given resources under our feet to fuel the technological revolution of the 21st century.

priorities.text: Lowering property tax bills for seniors.

positions.summary: Describes herself as pro-life with exceptions; did not list the exceptions at a January 2026 event.
positions.quote: My position on abortion has never changed: I am pro-life, but I am for exceptions.

record.text: As Treasurer, launched Money Match in 2025, which automatically mails checks to Pennsylvanians with unclaimed property without requiring a claim form; Treasury reports nearly $50 million sent through the program.
Treasury reports a record $334 million in unclaimed property returned in 2025 and more than $1 billion returned since she took office.
Treasury reports 546 military decorations returned to veterans and families during her tenure, including her 500th in 2025.

candidates.name: Ken Krawchuk
candidates.ballotNote: Libertarian nominee; running with John Thomas for lieutenant governor. Certified for the ballot, according to his campaign and Spotlight PA.

priorities.text: Veto all tax increases and phase out the personal income tax, per his 12-step platform.
End the state monopoly on education and abolish property taxes.
Eliminate parole for violent criminals and pardon all non-violent drug offenders.

positions.summary: Proposes giving every student a state-funded education savings account usable at any school.
positions.quote: Use current state funding to provide every student with an $11,500 Education Savings Account and let parents choose any school for their child.

positions.summary: Says passing more gun control laws would not help.
positions.quote: Passing more gun control laws would not help.

statements.quote: Defuse the abortion issue by allowing for Pre-Natal Adoption.
The fracking boom is good for Pennsylvania, but the property rights of the surrounding communities must be protected.
I promise to veto every single tax increase.
statements.context: On his campaign website, taxes page (a general pledge, not specific to high earners or corporations)

researchNotes: Ballotpedia blocked automated access during research. The Pennsylvania Department of State's certified candidate list could not be retrieved (Incapsula block, not bypassed). The slate is confirmed by the official general-election ballot published by Adams County's Board of Elections (Shapiro/Davis, Garrity/Richey, Krawchuk/Thomas; no Green ticket) and by independent reporting: Spotlight PA (Shapiro, Garrity and Krawchuk are the candidates on the ballot; Krawchuk is the only third-party candidate), LNP (Commonwealth Court removal of the Green ticket) and the Green Papers, with Wikipedia for primary results. Running mates Austin Davis (D), Jason Richey (R) and John Thomas (L) are elected jointly and are listed in ballotNote, not as separate entries. Shapiro, Garrity and Krawchuk are 'basic'. Shapiro's pa.gov bill-signing releases for individual bills were not used. Garrity's Treasury figures are Treasury's own reports for calendar 2025 and carry no specific date. Krawchuk is now 'basic': positions and statements come from the issue pages of his campaign website (kenk4pa.com); no minimum-wage, immigration or other positions were found there.
